On two disjoint product balls, take fields v, w, z with the fixed boundary values: w differs from v by one local Hopf modification in the first component, and z differs from w by one in the second. Then v is related to w and w to z, but v is not related to z: a single ball lies in one component, leaving a nontrivial relative Hopf difference in the other. Thus the stated relation is not transitive and does not define homology classes at this scope. The empty balanced manifold also has no ball witnessing reflexivity.
